evidence.paraphrase: Jerry reacts with fear and denial when confronted with the ghost.
evidence.quote:
Jerry's first impulse was to run like hell. "But I don't believe in
ghosts!"

evidence.paraphrase: The ghost states a rule that belief is a precondition for perceiving him.
evidence.quote: Of course you do. If you didn't, you couldn't have seen me.

evidence.paraphrase: The ghost describes an organized union structure governing ghosts and lighthouses.
evidence.quote:
As a ghost in
good standing, a dues-paying member of Asmodeus Local of the United
Lighthouse Haunters of America, Wully never done nothin' to deserve
this. Evicted!

evidence.paraphrase: A supernatural helper produces floating coals, introducing the presence of ghosts into the mundane setting.
evidence.quote:
Selecting
one, the stranger said, "Thank you, Junior. You can go now." He turned,
lit Jerry's cigarette and his own.

evidence.paraphrase: Rule explaining that ghostly materialization is a controllable act.
evidence.quote:
She could materialize if she wanted
to. She doesn't want to.

evidence.paraphrase: A stated periodicity governing when a particular spirit becomes visible.
evidence.quote: Celeste only materializes once every seven years.

evidence.paraphrase: The ghost explains bureaucratic-style eligibility rules limiting who can benefit from good luck.
evidence.quote: I'm not eligible. Employees, relatives etc.

evidence.paraphrase: Heather reacts with disorientation on witnessing the ghosts.
evidence.quote: "I think I'm losing my mind," she said.

evidence.paraphrase: Restatement of the rule that perceiving ghosts requires belief.
evidence.quote:
No matter what you
think, you couldn't see him if you didn't believe.

evidence.paraphrase: Ghostly intervention alters Jerry's paintings and creates new works, changing his artistic fortunes.
evidence.quote:
'Twas Junior touched up the
paintings. And 'twas Junior painted Gertrude.

evidence.paraphrase: The ghostly help leads to lasting fame and a body of celebrated work.
evidence.quote:
Meanwhile, what collector
hasn't heard of J. Masterson-Junior, whose canvases are lauded for
their "other world" quality?

evidence.paraphrase: A spirit explains the anatomy of a fantastical creature whose left legs are shorter, fitted with prosthetics.
A ghost supernaturally manipulates Wesley's necktie during the confrontation.
evidence.quote:
One end of the necktie became longer and longer as its opposite
end shortened. With a final but quiet jerk, the necktie came free,
hesitated for a moment opposite Wesley's belt buckle, then folded
itself neatly and floated away.

evidence.paraphrase: The community treats as a joke what the narrative has presented as real, contrasting outside perception with story facts.
evidence.quote:
Such a delightfully zany
couple! Always joking about a Scottish sea captain who lives in the
attic and is married to an Indian princess.
